reflection: This group contained a large number of administrative or storage-related codes (`s-pakaste`, `b-vara`, etc.) which are unmappable and were left empty. These are common in source data but represent pre-analytical or logistical steps, not observations. The `s-maksa*` and `s-afmaks*` series of codes were ambiguous, likely referring to different liver enzymes (ALT, AST) or alkaline phosphatase isoenzymes without being specific. I made educated guesses (e.g., mapping `maksa-1` to ALT) but this is a low-confidence mapping. Similarly, `p-varmtr` was obscure, and I had to guess a generic coagulation test. Having a more complete national codebook with mappings from these local abbreviations to official long names would resolve most of these ambiguities. The IgE allergy tests (`-pähe`, `-päe` suffixes) were quite clear, as were the therapeutic drug monitoring tests (carbamazepine, valproate). The variety of units for `S-Parvabg` (parvovirus IgG) demonstrates the importance of mapping each unit combination separately, as `titre`, `index` (Ratio), and `iu/ml` (Units/volume) all correspond to different LOINC properties.
